{
  "problem_id": "tmm_problem_cf712123ca1f601b",
  "planning_summary": "The problem defines a strictly constrained two-layer antireflection coating design space with only one genuine degree of freedom: the permutation of the two required materials (SiO2 and TiO2). Since the topology fixes the layer count to exactly two and the material set to exactly one of each, there are only two possible stack configurations: [Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass] and [Air/TiO2/SiO2/Glass]. These represent mutually exclusive discrete states; a single optimization route cannot tune 'order' as a continuous variable without becoming a combinatorial search that obscures which specific topology yielded the result. Therefore, the strategy selects the single most physically promising axis based on standard AR coating theory (gradient index matching) to maximize the probability of meeting the soft target within the limited evaluation budget. The chosen axis optimizes the thicknesses of the Low-High (SiO2-TiO2) configuration, hypothesizing that placing the lower index material first provides a smoother impedance transition from air to the high-index titania layer and finally to the glass substrate.",
  "routes": [
    {
      "route_id": "route_01",
      "title": "Optimization of SiO2/TiO2 Bilayer Order and Thickness for Broadband AR",
      "route_kind": "optimize_existing_stack",
      "scientific_hypothesis": "For a two-layer system with indices n_air < n_SiO2 < n_TiO2 > n_glass, the stack ordering Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass yields a lower global minimum mean reflectance than Air/TiO2/SiO2/Glass because the intermediate SiO2 layer reduces the initial impedance mismatch at the air interface more effectively than starting with the high-index TiO2.",
      "design_principle": "Impedance matching in multilayer optics suggests that arranging layers in ascending order of refractive index (or close to it) minimizes Fresnel reflections at each interface. Placing the lower index SiO2 (n=1.46) adjacent to air (n=1.0) creates a smaller step change than placing TiO2 (n=2.40) adjacent to air, potentially broadening the low-reflectance bandwidth despite the non-ideal final step from TiO2 to Glass (n=1.52).",
      "proposed_materials": [
        "sio2",
        "tio2"
      ],
      "proposed_topology": "Air (semi-infinite) / SiO2 (finite) / TiO2 (finite) / Glass (semi-infinite)",
      "design_variables": [
        "thickness of SiO2 layer (continuous, 40-160 nm)",
        "thickness of TiO2 layer (continuous, 40-160 nm)"
      ],
      "soft_objectives": [
        "minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (s-pol, normal incidence) over 450-700 nm",
        "achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a preference"
      ],
      "manufacturing_considerations": [
        "layer thicknesses must remain within 40 nm to 160 nm bounds",
        "exactly one layer of each material permitted"
      ],
      "evidence_ids": [],
      "theory_basis": [
        "Fresnel equations for normal incidence reflection at dielectric interfaces",
        "Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) for calculating coherent superposition of fields in stratified media",
        "Quarter-wave transformer theory generalized for broadband minimization via numerical optimization"
      ],
      "expected_advantages": [
        "Directly tests the theoretically preferred material ordering for impedance grading",
        "Concentrates the limited 64-evaluation budget on refining thicknesses for the most promising topology rather than splitting resources between two topologies",
        "Provides a clear baseline; if this optimal ordering fails to meet the target, the reverse ordering is unlikely to succeed given the larger initial index mismatch"
      ],
      "known_risks": [
        "The reverse order (TiO2/SiO2) might unexpectedly perform better due to specific phase cancellation effects at the substrate interface not captured by simple impedance arguments",
        "The thickness constraints (40-160 nm) may prevent the formation of ideal quarter-wave or half-wave conditions for the entire 450-700 nm band",
        "Constant index assumption may introduce errors if actual material dispersion is significant, though the problem statement mandates constant indices"
      ],
      "execution_request_english": "Execute a deterministic Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) optimization for a planar four-medium stack: Air (n=1.0), Layer 1 (SiO2, n=1.46), Layer 2 (TiO2, n=2.40), Substrate (Glass, n=1.52). The optimization must vary the thickness of the SiO2 layer and the TiO2 layer independently, subject to hard bounds of 40 nm to 160 nm for each. The objective function is the arithmetic mean of the power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence (0 degrees), calculated at 5 nm intervals from 450 nm to 700 nm inclusive. Use a deterministic optimizer with seed 17, allowing a maximum of 64 solver evaluations. Report the best candidate's thicknesses, the full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Do not use RCWA, FDFD, or surrogate models.",
      "priority": 1,
      "parent_route_id": null,
      "revision_reason": null,
      "expected_observations": [
        "If the hypothesis holds, the optimizer should converge to a solution where best_target_score approaches 1.0 (corresponding to mean reflectance near 0.0) or at least significantly improves over unoptimized guesses, with tightest_margin remaining positive relative to the 40/160 nm bounds.",
        "If the hypothesis fails or the constraints are too tight, best_target_score will plateau at a lower value corresponding to a mean reflectance above 0.03, and valid_candidates may cluster near the boundary limits (40 or 160 nm) indicating the solver is pushing against constraints.",
        "The reflectance spectrum should show a broad dip centered roughly in the 450-700 nm range if successful, or a narrow/shifted dip if the thickness constraints limit performance."
      ],
      "stop_conditions": [
        "If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-4 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds of evaluation (within the 64 eval limit), treat the local optimum as found, stop the search, and retain the current best thickness pair.",
        "If the optimizer exhausts the 64 solver evaluations without converging to a stable point, stop and report the best valid candidate found so far.",
        "If all generated candidates violate the 40-160 nm thickness constraints (valid_candidates = 0), stop and flag the constraint set as infeasible for this topology."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "research_influence": [],
  "unresolved_decisions": [
    "Whether the reverse topology (Air/TiO2/SiO2/Glass) should be tested in a subsequent study if route_01 fails to achieve a mean reflectance below 0.05, as the current budget allows only one route."
  ],
  "stop_if_all_routes_fail": "If the single executed route yields a mean reflectance greater than 0.05 despite exhaustive tuning within bounds, conclude that a two-layer system with these specific materials and thickness constraints is insufficient to meet the 0.03 target, and recommend expanding the design space to three layers or relaxing thickness limits in future work."
}
